data.about: The Essing timber bridge as one continuous funicular band over fields of 17 + 32.5 + 32.5 + 17 m. The deck weight, cut into 1.7 m strips, hangs the main field from a pole fixed by the support tangent and the horizontal crown tangent; the approach field has the same geometry mirrored, so its loads are laid off upward on the load line (Fₗ = −Fᵣ) and the band runs kink-free over the pier. The vertical through the pole gives the trestle reaction A, the abutment tangent the anchor pull Fₗ with horizontal component H; the right half follows by symmetry, and the whole band resolves in tension.

steps.caption: the Essing bridge: a timber band over 17 + 32.5 + 32.5 + 17 m — trestle bents under the approaches, the canal under the main span
steps.title: The site

steps.caption: left: the deck weight q as strips of 1.7 m on the half main field, resultant R₁/₂ — right: the 20 strip loads stacked on the load line
steps.title: The load on the main field

steps.caption: left: chord and tangents of the parabola — support tangent and horizontal crown tangent meet over the quarter line (drag the crown!) — right: parallels through the load-line ends meet at the pole o₁
steps.title: Crown point and tangents → pole o₁

steps.caption: left: from the pier, one string per strip, parallel to the rays — through the crown — right: the fan of rays to o₁
steps.title: The funicular of the main field

steps.caption: right: the last ray is the horizontal force H, the first ray the tangent force F at the pier — left: the same two forces on the band
steps.title: H at the crown, F at the pier

steps.caption: left: the approach has the SAME geometry mirrored, so its q acts reversed (band below the deck): Fₗ = −Fᵣ — right: its 10 loads are laid off UPWARD from the start of the load line, resultant R₂
steps.title: The approach field: loads laid off upward

steps.caption: left: abutment tangent and pier tangent meet over the middle of the field — right: the parallel through the top of the reversed loads meets the pier-tangent ray at o₂
steps.title: Tangents of the approach → pole o₂

steps.caption: left: from the abutment, one string per strip — the band arches UP over the trestles and runs kink-free over the pier — right: its fan of rays to o₂
steps.title: The funicular of the approach field

steps.caption: right: the vertical through o₁ cuts the abutment-tangent line at N₇: A = o₁–N₇ — left: the trestles push the arching band up with A
steps.title: The trestle reaction A

steps.caption: right: N₇ to the top of the reversed loads closes the polygon: Fₗ — left: the abutment anchors the band along its tangent
steps.title: The anchor force Fₗ

steps.caption: right: the horizontal component of the anchor force is exactly H, the vertical rest is Fₗᵥ — the polygon H + A + Fₗ + R₂ + R₁/₂ closes
steps.title: Components of Fₗ

steps.caption: both sides: the same construction mirrored in grey — reaction B at the right trestles, anchor Fᵣ at the right abutment
steps.title: The right half by symmetry

steps.caption: the continuous band works in TENSION everywhere (pink) — H is constant through all fields; pipes show the force; drag the crown or the sliders
steps.title: The band resolves
